pages.text: The Eternal Youth is a consumable item that - quite simply put - imbues the animal it's used on with a never ending state of immortality as a youngling. If the animal in question is not currently young, it will be reverted to its youth. The immortality given is near absolute; the few ways of killing such an animal is either to lose it to the void or to use a second Eternal Youth on them.

It's quite an arduous process to craft it, as it requires some exotic eggs and animals. Yet, if you don't ever want to let go of your most loyal pets, these exotics are a cheap sacrifice to avoid such a sad future.

pages.title: Addendum
pages.text: Recently, a realization has been haunting me. It came about suddenly, as if long unresolved puzzle pieces finally got put together... When it comes to the plague, be it creating life; sustaining or elongating an existing one; or even rebirthing it from death - it's clear that the Risus celebrates life. Even beyond that, it gives life freely, without any deals or tricks. As well as that - although it pains me to admit - it also

gives the choice of whether or not to accept its gift. It is true that the Offsprings also take life, including other creations of the plague; yet none of those cases are directly done so by the Risus. It gives life to anyone and anything, even if the receiver of the gift will end up taking another one's life. The plague simply answers the desire of any who dare ask it; with no malevolence involved. At the same time, if someone asks for the death of another, the plague will not directly cause

it, but it will still give the necessary power of violence to the inquirer. The Risus loves life, and does not wish for death... But this isn't what actually haunts me. It's the fact that I am starting to view the plague more positively - even slowly embracing it. I knew this could happen; it's the risk that comes with understanding what should be feared. Yet, it really scares me. Even if I can still see the line clearly, when will the moment come when I will be no different from the cultist

raiders I've come across? It would be foolish to say that because of my morality I would always be better than them. I'm sure they too believe to be in the right, despite the atrocities they commit. That's the realization that haunts me: soon, I might not be any better than the deranged cultists drunk on having been assimilated with the plague.
